findings.title: Check-then-open introduces a race that can overwrite a concurrently created file
findings.evidence: The new logic first checks for existence and then opens the path in write mode, so another process or thread can create the file after the check but before the open; on POSIX, 'w' will truncate that file instead of failing, losing data that the previous 'x' mode protected against.
findings.recommendation: Keep atomic creation by using exclusive mode again, e.g. 'open(path, "x")', or use os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and wrap the fd. Do not split existence checking from creation.
